MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-15, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service: Utilizes Global Integrated Base Plan tools and data for global management of the total Joint Force and development of National Defense strategy and joint warfighting capabilities. Applies knowledge of joint operations, joint doctrine and tactics, techniques and procedures to provide recommendations, guidance, and priorities to senior leaders on Global Force Management (GFM) programs. Plans and analyzes operational planning, global force management and strategy development for complex issues within integrated cross-functional teams and Combatant Commands (CCMDs). Creates program forces assessments utilizing Planning, Programming, Budgeting and Executing System (PPBES), Acquisition System, and/or Joint Strategic Planning System for mid-and long- term effects on all Department components. Substitution of education may not be used in lieu of specialized experience for this grade level. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for leading the development of the Department's Force Management Framework and associated Directed Readiness Tables, as well as identifying and analyzing the required forces related to Force Assignment Tables
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-8 Directorate (Force Structure, Resources & Assessment) is charged with providing support to CJCS for evaluating and developing force structure requirements. J-8 conducts joint, bilateral, and multilateral war games and interagency politico-military seminars and simulations. It develops, maintains, and improves the models, techniques, and capabilities used by the Joint Staff and combatant commands to conduct studies and analyses for CJCS.
MajorDuties: As a STRATEGIC ANALYST OPS PLANNER at the GS-0301-15 some of your typical work assignments may include: Directs and manages the development and execution of all Global Force Management Implementation Guidance, Directed Readiness Tables, and Force Assignment Tables for the Secretary of Defense. Design, planning and productivity of a Department of Defense team comprised of force management experts from multiple Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Combatant Commands (CCMDs) and Department of Defense Components. Serves as principal and senior technical expert, analyst, and advisor to the senior most Joint Staff leadership on all joint force management matters related to DoD force assignment to Military Secretaries and CCMDs to include past and current Office of the Secretary of Defense Joint Staff (JS) policy decisions. Responsible for leading, and participating in, efforts spanning the planning, development, maintenance, production, and integration of Global Force Management strategic-level reform and initiatives that are aligned with the strategy and senior leader guidance. Assists Joint Staff lead for planning, organizing and executing CJCS Senior Seminar Series activities for the Department's senior-most leaders, intended to provide the Department's senior leadership with operational force management capability and capacity assessments through tabletop exercises designed to examine the Department's strategic force development policy and force planning issues. Responsible for gaining consensus where appropriate amongst the Department's senior most leadership, finding compromise positions and brokering agreeable decisions between Joint Staff offices, OSD staff & agencies, Combatant Commands and Service representatives.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Will be responsible for Joint Policy advice, development, maintenance, and support, to inform senior decision makers regarding global petroleum matters. Will afford joint logistics enterprise command and control governance through representation and collaboration with the Office of Secretary of Defense (OSD), Combatant Commands (CCMDs), Military Departments, and the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-4 (Logistics,) leads the logistics enterprise, drive joint force readiness and provide the best logistics advice to the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, to maximize the joint force commander's freedom of action.
MajorDuties: As a SENIOR STRATEGIC ANALYST (PETROLEUM) at the GS-0301-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Actively assesses the impact of policies and legislation on the integration efforts across the global U.S. Department of Defense petroleum supply chain. Analyzes and evaluates legislative proposals for potential impact on DoD petroleum supply and distribution programs. Analyzes management issues and problems, and resolves matters with relevant leadership members and senior subject matter experts. Manages and validates Joint Staff Bulk Petroleum Contingency Reports (REPOL), Bulk Petroleum Capabilities Report (POLCAP), Petroleum War Reserve Requirement (PWRR), Pre­Positioned War Reserve Stock (PWRS), Days of Supply (DOS) Guidance, the Inventory Management Plan (IMP), and various Situation Reports (SITREPs). Serves as the Combatant Commander's advocate in petroleum policy and doctrinal matters with a thorough understanding of and sensitivity to the needs of the joint force. Evaluates alternative strategies for solving daily analytic issues to fmd both technical and non-technical, cost-effective solutions

In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes developing and recommending material requirements; overseeing fielding plans and force modernization activities; assisting with the development of the Program Objective Memorandum (POM) and Extended Planning Period (EPP) material/monetary requirements for assigned systems; converting senior leader guidance into program and budget instructions for systems. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-13). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas:
Oral CommunicationOrganizational Performance AnalysisRequirements Analysis
Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-13).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as Synchronization Staff Officer (SSO), Action Officer (AO), and principal representative for G-8, Force Development Directorate in matters pertaining to one or more assigned systems. Manages those assigned systems to ensure manpower, money, and material resources are properly allocated to support timely development, procurement, and fielding of new items and appropriate cascading of replaced items.
Details.SubAgencyName: Deputy Chief of Staff G-8, Force Development, Directorate of Materiel
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Assist with developing strategy and justification of resources to support system requirements to Army leadership, Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Office of Management and Budget (OMB), and Congress, resulting in funding of programs.
Coordinate with leadership to obtain program support and to ensure program success.
Assist with new acquisition strategies to meet established priorities for assigned systems.
Coordinate with Organizational Integrators to ensure force structure and hardware fielding is compatible.
Analyze and identify potential for joint programs with other Services and allied nations and make recommendations for programs.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for directing and overseeing the development, implementation, assessment, and refinement of strategies, plans, and policies to support the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (CJCS) to fulfill his global military integration function.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-5 (Strategic Plans and Policy) proposes strategies, plans, and policy recommendations to the CJCS to support his provision of "military advice" across the full spectrum of national security concerns to the President and other national leaders and to ensure those recommendations are informed by a larger strategic context coordinated with interagency and alliance partners, account for the view and requirements of the combatant commanders, and assess risk in executing the National Military Strategy.
MajorDuties: As a STRATEGIC PLANNER at the GS-0301-15 some of your typical work assignments may include: This position represents the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (CJCS) for all matters relating to strategies, plans and policies in support of the CJCS statutory global military integration function. This position is required to regularly interact with General Officer/Flag Officer and Senior Executive Service members within DoD, various US Government Departments and Agencies (such as the Departments of State, Homeland Security, Treasury and the National Counterterrorism Center), as well as with key U.S. Ally and Partner nations. Uses analytical judgment to review, and initiates changes to military strategies, policies and procedures to ensure that the Joint Force has sufficient capacity and capability to achieve National Defense Strategy (NDS), and National Military Strategy (NMS) objectives. Conduct research, compose and present position papers, and manage and lead supporting projects and programs to completion.

Details.JobSummary: Please read this Public Notice in its entirety. Instructions on how to apply can be found in the "How to Apply Section." Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: If you want to do interesting and challenging work and to make a contribution to national defense, DISA is a great place for you. DISA provides secure and reliable communications and computing support that enable the President and our military forces to communicate globally through voice, video, and data transmission. DISA is a leader within the Federal Government in implementing "people programs" and offers a broad range of quality-of-life and training programs. Go to www.disa.mil for more information. This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. Positions in the Cyber Excepted Service are positions necessary to carry out and support the mission of the United States Cyber Command.
MajorDuties: Serve as a Program Analyst within the Joint Service Provider (JSP), Business Resource Center, Acquisition Division, supporting the agency?s Information Technology acquisition program.
Engage in program-related data collection and analysis; assisting JSP requirement owners and stakeholders in defining, documenting, planning, and execution of requirements.
Participate in the development of acquisition strategy and development of acquisition packages.

Liaise with contracting organizations regarding the completion and award of service contracts, post award Contracting Officer?s Representative services, including contract compliance management, performance evaluation, and contract closeout support.

Provide an essential service by integrating technical aspects with program management and contractual matters, including planning and scheduling, budgeting, expenditure accounting, and program analysis reporting.
Perform continuing analyses of the effectiveness, efficiency, cost effectiveness, schedule adherence, and other key parameters of the acquisition program?s progress and success.
Assist in the development, documentation, and improvement of business processes, procedures and best practices. Based on analytical results and reports, identify potential problem areas.

Prepare and coordinate program budget requests, justifications, and other financial planning documents that are fully defensible and adhere to governing Army, DoD, and Federal Directives, policies and regulations.

Therefore, to the extent a Federal job announcement includes the requirement that applicants must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 pursuant to E.O. 14043, that requirement does not currently apply. For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the length of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume? at https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include/ You may qualify at the NH-04 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the NH-3 (or GS-13) grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability researching, analyzing, and synthesizing conflicting information and data to formulate policies and procedures governing congressional affairs; and to respond to legislative inquiries. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Submit a copy of your applicable SF-50, along with a statement that provides the following information regarding your most recent political appointment: Position title; Type of appointment (Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES, or Presidential Appointee); Agency; and, Beginning and ending dates of appointment.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering (OUSD (R&E)). The USD(R&E) serves as the Chief Technology Officer and is responsible for research, development, and prototyping activities within the Department of Defense (DoD).
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research & Engineering (USD(R&E))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as the Chief Technology Officer and is responsible for research, development, and prototyping activities within the Department of Defense (DoD); Facilitates open lines of communication and understanding, maintaining and/or establishing close working relationships with the OUSD (R&E) Front Office, Deputy Chief Technology Officers (DCTO) and Principal Directors, Directors, USD(R&E) Staff Principals, ASD Legislative Affairs (OSD(LA)), USD Comptroller Budget Affairs and Activity (BAA) Office, JCS Legislative Liaison, and legislative liaison offices of military Services; Works with OSD(LA) and BAA to maintain and update appropriate biographical information on all Members of the House or Senate and key congressional staff, including the Members most current research and engineering interests and concerns; Ensures all House or Senate activities (trips, meetings, and hearings) are communicated to OUSD(R&E) and senior leaders in a timely manner; Ensures Senior OUSD(R&E) leaders are aware of key decision points so that they can affect the process at the right time and place; Provides assistance at hearings of congressional committees and bodies, analyzes discussions from these meetings and outlines the concerns and issues that may require incorporation into the OUSD and DCTO's congressional communication engagement strategy.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume? at https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include/ You may qualify at the GS-14 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to conduct policy compliance reviews and serve on special committees or groups in support of policy and legislative requirements (e.g., Executive Order working groups, policy compliance review teams, etc.). Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Submit a copy of your applicable SF-50, along with a statement that provides the following information regarding your most recent political appointment: Position title; Type of appointment (Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES, or Presidential Appointee); Agency; and, Beginning and ending dates of appointment. All qualifications and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located within the Office of Force Resiliency (OFR), which falls under the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (OUSD(P&R)). Its mission OFR is to strengthen and promote the resiliency and readiness of the Total Force by developing integrated policies, oversight, and synchronization of activities in the areas of diversity management, personnel risk reduction, suicide/sexual assault prevention, and collaborative efforts with the Dept. of Veterans Affairs.
Details.SubAgencyName: Off. of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (OUSD (Personnel and Readiness))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Supports integrated prevention programs and associated program requirements and objectives, such as Department of Defense (DoD) agencies, the Military Departments and Services, OUSD (P&R), Office of Force Resiliency (OFR), VA, interagency meetings, and topic-specific groups covering integrated prevention, and/or issues relevant to the missions and objectives of OFR. Develops strategic, programmatic, and policy recommendations, and provides evidence-based rationale for integrated prevention program recommendations. Develops, coordinates, and finalizes recommendations for policy inputs impacting DoD and Military Department and Service regulatory guidance. Develops, reviews, and provides feedback and coordination on briefs, information papers, and other strategic communication materials. Reviews, analyzes, and edits annual and special reports OFR submits to various entities and ensures they articulate all reporting requirements; supports OFR's congressional/legislative work including staffing, research, analysis, and formulation of official responses to from Members of Congress, their staffs, and congressional committees. Monitors the Defense Appropriation and Authorization Bill processes, including subcommittee and committee hearings, deliberations on the House and Senate floors, and passage into Public Law.
Details.Education: Education cannot be substituted for experience.
Details.Evaluations: Once the announcement has closed, a review of your résumé and supporting documentation will be used to determine whether you meet the qualification requirements listed on this announcement. If you are minimally qualified, your résumé and supporting documentation will be compared against your responses to the assessment questionnaire to determine your level of experience. If, after reviewing your résumé and/or supporting documentation, a determination is made that you have inflated your qualifications and/or experience, you may lose consideration for this position. Please follow all instructions carefully when applying, errors or omissions may affect your eligibility. All qualified candidates will be assigned to a quality category. The category assignment is a measure of the degree in which your background matches the competencies required for this position. Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your responses to the assessment questionnaire. The assessment questionnaire link can be found under the 'How To Apply' section. Decision MakingInterpersonal SkillOrganizational AwarenessPolicy DevelopmentStrategic Planning Effective 5/25/2022, we will use the resume's employment dates and grade information in conjunction with the provided SF-50 at the lower grade level to give credit for time in grade requirements. We will confirm time in grade at the job offer stage if needed. At a minimum, you are still required to provide an SF-50 at the lower grade level for promotion eligibility consideration when applying for a promotion for GS-positions. PPP PILOT: The Washington Headquarters Service is currently operating under an approved reengineered Priority Placement Program (PPP) pilot for all positions in its serviced workforce. This pilot is application based and current PPP registrants who are registered for activity codes 293A and 295A (regardless of the location) are required to apply to the job announcement via USAJobs in order to exercise their priority placement status. This pilot permits priority candidates to be assessed with other competitive applicants. Anyone claiming priority status must provide a copy of their PPP registration and supporting documentation (e.g. RIF notice, Certification of Expected Separation) at the time of application to verify priority placement and eligibility. MILITARY SPOUSE PREFERENCE: Military spouse preference applicants are required to apply to job announcement via USAJobs in order to exercise their preference status. The application must include signed Military Spouse PPP Self-Certification Checklist, Marriage Certificate or License, Sponsor's PCS orders at the time of application to be considered. MSP applicants will receive priority consideration at the FPL, and if selected, will be placed at the FPL. Other priority consideration programs will continue under their current operating procedures.
Details.HowToApply: To apply for this position, you must complete the online application and submit the documentation specified in the Required Documents section below. A complete application package must be submitted by 11:59 PM (EST) on the closing date of the announcement (08/15/2022) to receive consideration. If you do not have a USAJOBS account, you will need to create one before beginning the application. You will have the opportunity to upload additional documents to include in your application before it is submitted. Your uploaded documents may take several hours to clear the virus scan process. After acknowledging you have reviewed your application package, complete the Include Personal Information section as you deem appropriate and click to continue with the application process. You will be taken to the online application which you must complete in order to apply for the position. Complete the online application, verify the required documentation is included with your application package, and submit the application. To view the assessment questionnaire, click here: https://apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/11586573 To verify the status of your application, log into your USAJOBS account (https://my.usajobs.gov/Account/Login) all of your applications will appear on the Welcome screen. The Application Status will appear along with the date your application was last updated. For information on what each Application Status means, visit: https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/how-to/application/status/. You are encouraged to apply online. Applying online will allow you to review and track the status of your application. Do not email or send hard copy resumes/applications to the Contact Information or Agency Information listed in this vacancy announcement. All resumes/applications received at the addresses listed in the Contact Information or Agency Information will be destroyed and will not be considered for this vacancy announcement. It is the applicant's responsibility to verify that all information in their resume and documents are legible and accurate. HR will not modify answers/documents submitted by an applicant. Washington Headquarters Services provides reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application and hiring process, please view the "Alternate Application" method listed in the "Other Information" section of this announcement. Your requests for reasonable accommodation will be addressed on a case-by-case basis. Details.RequiredDocuments:
YOU ARE REQUIRED TO DOCUMENT IN YOUR APPLICATION PACKAGE EVIDENCE THAT SUPPORTS YOUR ELIGIBILITY AND QUALIFICATION CLAIMS. You MUST upload the applicable documents with your application package. If you fail to provide these documents, you will be marked as having an incomplete application package and you will not be considered any further. 1. Your resume may be submitted in any format that includes your name and contact information (telephone number and/or email).
If you submit more than one copy of your resume, only the most recent version will be reviewed. The latest timestamp will be used to determine which version of your resume is "most recent." If your resume includes a photograph or other inappropriate material or content, it will not be used to make eligibility and qualification determinations and you will not be considered for this vacancy. Are you applying for a promotion? If you are a current or former Federal Civilian employee and applying for a higher grade than the grade that you currently or formerly held within the last 52 weeks, it is recommended you provide SF-50(s) that show you have held the next lower grade for at least one year. Some SF-50s effective within the last 52 weeks will not demonstrate you have held the next lower grade for at least one year (e.g. General Adjustment SF-50 from this year). In many cases, you are required to provide two (2) SF-50s to determine you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirement and eligibility for promotion.
Examples of appropriate SF-50s include: Appointment or Promotion SF-50 AND another SF-50 with an effective date on or after one year from the appointment or promotion at the same grade level; Within-Grade Increase (WGI) SF-50s showing regular step increase received for the same grade, etc. It is still recommended you provide a Within-Grade Increase (WGI) SF-50 or multiple SF-50's at least one year apart at the lower grade level for time in grade confirmation with your application. 2. Other supporting documents: Cover Letter, optional Most recent SF-50 "Notification of Personnel Action" showing you are/were in the competitive service and the highest grade held. It is recommended you provide a SF-50 within the last 52 weeks before the closing date of this JOA for current federal employees. Effective 5/25/2022, WHS HRD will use the resume in conjunction with the provided SF-50 to confirm Current Federal Employee eligibility. We will complete confirmation of Current Federal Employee eligibility at the job offer phase if needed. It is still required that you submit at least one SF-50 with your application and confirm you are a current federal employee via your employment dates on your resume for current federal employee eligibility determinations. (WHS serviced employees SF-50s can be verified via eOPF). 1. Details.OtherInformation: COVID-19 Vaccination: To ensure compliance with an applicable preliminary nationwide injunction, which may be supplemented, modified, or vacated, depending on the course of ongoing litigation, the Federal Government will take no action to implement or enforce the COVID-19 vaccination requirement pursuant to Executive Order 14043 on Requiring Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination for Federal Employees. Therefore, to the extent a Federal job announcement includes the requirement that applicants must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 pursuant to E.O. 14043, that requirement does not currently apply. Federal agencies may request information regarding the vaccination status of selected applicants for the purposes of implementing other workplace safety protocols, such as protocols related to masking, physical distancing, testing, travel, and quarantine. A tentative offer of employment will be rescinded if the selectee fails to meet the pre-employment requirements, including failure to report to any of the scheduled appointments. If you are unable to apply online, you must request an alternative application. To receive selection priority for this position, you must: (1) meet CTAP or ICTAP eligibility criteria; (2) be rated well-qualified for the position with a score of 85 or above; and, (3) submit the appropriate documentation to support your CTAP or ICTAP eligibility. For more information visit: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/employee-guide-to-career-transition/ Employed Annuitants (Reemployed Annuitants): Applicants in receipt of an annuity based on civilian employment in the Federal Service are subject to the DoD Policy on The Employment of Annuitants. http://www.esd.whs.mil/DD/DoD-Issuances/140025/ Nepotism: Under the provisions of 5 USC 3110, an individual may not be appointed into a position if the position is under the supervisory chain of command of a relative. Additional vacancies may be filled by this announcement.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Washington Headquarters Services (WHS) and serves as the chief of administration to the Director of History and Library (HLD). These organizations provide a full range of publications, historical research, and library services to the Office of the Secretary of Defense and specified Department of Defense Components. Duties require a thorough knowledge of the roles and responsibilities, priorities, goals and objectives of WHS and DoD generally.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Washington Headquarters Services (WHS) is a world-class service organization, with a dynamic workforce and unwavering commitment to service excellence. WHS is the essential services provider for the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Department of Defense (DoD) agencies, and offices in the National Capital Region
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Develops, interprets, and implements policies and procedures to provide oversight, planning, programming, and budget guidance to facilitate the identification and determination of alternative ways to achieve the best mix of people and support attainable, within fiscal constraints, for major mission and operational plans. Reviews and approves administrative materials submitted to the Director to ensure positions are well-reasoned, thoroughly staffed, and information is complete, current, accurate, and properly coordinated. Responsible for Pentagon Library Contract Administration/Management including all actions pertaining to contract award contract management, development of functional specifications, evaluation of contractor performance, termination or close­out of Firm Fixed Price, and Time & Material contracts. Maintains a continuous liaison with other WHS and OSD, other service counterparts, and DoD offices lo ensure planning is consistent and integrated throughout the defense community. Prepares and presents high-level briefings.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary:
In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Group Coverage Qualification Standard for Administrative and Management Positions SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Your resume must reflect the quality level of experience which demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for successful job performance required for this position. Examples of creditable experience include: Analyzing
effectiveness of current operations and proposes strategies for productivity enhancements, optimal organization structures, and effective resource allocation for JIOWC operational plans and objectives; Establishes and maintains relationships by liaising with key organizations; and Advising and proves counsel to employees regarding policies, procedures, and directives of management. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Expert knowledge of Information Operations, intelligence, and military operations and Mastery knowledge of CCMD operations and agency disciplines to identify specific issues requiring trans-regional, multi-agency, and multi-disciplinary solutions. Mastery knowledge of the Joint Planning and Execution Community, the Joint Operation Planning Process, and resource planning. Knowledge of all Joint Information Operations functional disciplines and intimate knowledge of current JOWC responsibilities/capabilities, and the relationship with JS, OSD, CCMDs, and other agencies. Knowledge of management principle, processes, and analytical techniques for assessing programs; expertise in developing strategies for operational improvements and efficiencies. Skill in establishing and maintaining effective relationships, building consensus and coalitions, negotiating, and resolving conflict. Skill in oral and written communication and experience delivering information to senior leaders. Ability to effectively organize and analyze information; produce reports, position papers, and briefings that meet the specific needs of senior management officials/senior leaders; present clear and concise findings; resolve conflicts based on mature judgement, experience, and recognized professional standing; and effectively advocate for a position. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and mentor, motivate, and appraise the staff of an organization through subordinate supervisors. OTHER SIGNIFICANT FACTS: Position is designated special-sensitive and requires eligibility for access to Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), other intelligence-related Special Sensitive information, or involvement in Top Secret Special Access Programs (SAP) to fully perform the duties and responsibilities of the position. A non-disclosure agreement must be signed. Drug Testing: This position has been designated by the Air Force as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Demand Reduction Program. Employee must pass initial and periodic short notice drug testing. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety. Key: The duties of this position meets all requirements as a category 4 designation, and shall not be vacated during a national emergency or mobilization without seriously impairing the capability of the parent Federal Agency or office to function effectively. This position must be removed from the Ready Reserve and CAN NOT become a member of the Ready Reserve. (IAW: DoDD 1200.7, "Screening the Ready Reserve,") Mobility: Mobility is a condition of employment. The employee must sign an Air Force-wide mobility agreement. (Note: See AFI36-202, dated 19 Aug 2019 for guidance) Polygraph: Incumbent is required to undergo a counterintelligence-scope polygraph examination. The employee may be required to travel in military and/or commercial aircraft to perform temporary duty assignments. The employee may be required to work other than normal duty hours, which may include evenings, weekends, and/or holidays. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. This position is a Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel Systems (DCIPS) position implemented under Section 504, Title V of Public Law 99-569, Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1987, as codified in Sec 1601, Chap 83 of Title 10 United States Code which sets forth Air Force policies and procedures for DCIPS. This position is in the Excepted Service. DoD Components with DCIPS positions apply Veterans' Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 2005, DCIPS Employment and Placement. If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. For additional information on DCIPS, click here
MajorDuties: As Director of Operations, manages and oversees functions responsible for the analysis, evaluation, and implementation of effective programs in JIOWC operations, intelligence, and OPSEC areas. Analyzes effectiveness of current operations and proposes strategies for productivity enhancements, optimal organization structures, and effective resource allocation for JIOWC operational plans and objectives. Conducts mission-related coordination and builds coalitions with NCR- and CCMD-based organizations and leads integration of the Information Joint Function in plans across OSD, JS, and other organizations. Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities. Selects or recommends selection of candidates for vacancies, promotions, details, and reassignments in consideration of skills and qualifications, mission requirements, and EEO and diversity objectives. Implements approved operations policies, directives and plans. Analyzes and interprets applicable regulations, directives, and documents and ensures that organizational directives and policy instruments are consistent with these directives.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.

Prepare and oversee preparation of executive correspondence, presentation materials, briefings, assessments and proposals.
Maintain effective oversight of the Armys Primary Prevention System that encompasses human resources, collaborative relationships and infrastructure.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as a senior program analyst, participates and provides expertise in all aspects of the Army Planning, Programming, and Budgeting and Execution (PPBE) with special emphasis on the Program Objective Memorandum (POM) for continuity and effective management of assigned MM PEG programs. Works under the administrative direction of the Deputy, Resources Division who responds to the Chief, Resources Division, Director, Plans and Resources, Deputy Chief of Staff, G-1.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Manipulate and analyze data with complex structure using spreadsheets (excel pivot tables) and analytic software packages (such as tableau, minitab, sas, etc.).
Access and query data in data warehoused.
Load data and generate reports through defined user interface and business intelligence tools.
Research historic files and audit transaction history to provide forensic analysis of fiscal transactions.
Provide Army Senior Leaders and Commanders with simple, easily understandable narratives that they can articulate.
Perform detailed analysis, to include modeling and forecasting, in a high stakes, time constrained environment.

Utilize knowledge of the Federal Budget process, congressional committee structure as it relates to the Department of Defense (DoD) PPBE process, legislative process dealing with defense authorization and appropriations.

For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the length of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume? at https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include/ You may qualify at the GS-14 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement:
One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to: 1) demonstrating skills to conduct independent research and analysis of highly complex policy, strategy, concepts and program issues, force posture alternatives, and implications of broad changes to Command, control, communications, and computers (C4I) and related programs, 2) applying knowledge of Service C4I systems, networks, policies, organizations, and relationships, AND 3) demonstrating C4I domain technical, operational, and strategic analytical skills that can be applied to development of doctrine, organization, training, materiel, leadership, personnel, and facilities (DOTmLPF) associated with the federal government and its forces. You may qualify at the GS-15 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement:
One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to: 1) demonstrating skills to conduct independent research and analysis of highly complex policy, strategy, concepts and program issues, force posture alternatives, and implications of broad changes to Command, control, communications, and computers (C4I) and related programs (2) applying knowledge of Service C4I systems, networks, policies, organizations, and relationships. 3) demonstrating C4I domain technical, operational, and strategic analytical skills that can be applied to development of doctrine, organization, training, materiel, leadership, personnel, and facilities (DOTmLPF) associated with the federal government and its forces, AND 4) developing recommendations to support an Agency's decision-making process, including those related to program analysis, or capabilities development. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Submit a copy of your applicable SF-50, along with a statement that provides the following information regarding your most recent political appointment: Position title; Type of appointment (Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES, or Presidential Appointee); Agency; and, Beginning and ending dates of appointment. All qualifications and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. COVID-19 Vaccination: To ensure compliance with an applicable preliminary nationwide injunction, which may be supplemented, modified, or vacated, depending on the course of ongoing litigation, the Federal Government will take no action to implement or enforce the COVID-19 vaccination requirement pursuant to Executive Order 14043 on Requiring Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination for Federal Employees. Therefore, to the extent a Federal job announcement includes the requirement that applicants must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 pursuant to E.O. 14043, that requirement does not currently apply. Federal agencies may request information regarding the vaccination status of selected applicants for the purposes of implementing other workplace safety protocols, such as protocols related to masking, physical distancing, testing, travel, and quarantine.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict (OASD(SO/LIC)). The ASD(SO/LIC) serves as the principal advisor and assistant to the Secretary of Defense and has statutory responsibility for overseeing special operations-peculiar administrative matters pertaining to the readiness and organization of special operations forces (SOF), resources and equipment, and civilian personnel.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Secretary of Defense (OUSD Policy)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Conducts evaluations of programs and operational processes involving special operations Command, Control, Communications, Computers and Intelligence (C4I) forces using a variety of qualitative and quantitative methods to provide advice and recommendations to superiors to improve efficiency and effectiveness throughout the organization. Develops, coordinates, manages, and represents DoD policies and programs related to Service-Secretary-like oversight of USSOCOM's special operations C4I forces. Participates and assists in the presentation of OSD policies and budgets to DoD, Congress, other USG agencies, and the general public. Plays a major role in the study, review, evaluation and adjustment of the strategies, concepts, special operations C4I programs, and budgets required to support OSD policy and program planning guidance

Details.JobSummary:
The DCIO (SAP IT) is a direct report to the DoD CIO that leads, directs, and manages a staff comprised of senior executive service
(SES), civilian, military, and contractor personnel, providing expert management and oversight of the SAP IT enterprise, including
capabilities, architecture, requirements, cybersecurity, policy, governance, oversight and business operations to satisfy warfighter
SAP needs.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Department of Defense Chief Information Officer
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Responsible for the programmatic aspects of resource management in the annual planning, programming, budgeting, and execution (PPBE) cycle as it relates to the areas under the DCIO SAP IT purview and across the DoD SAP community. Developing, implementing, and continuously improving DCIO SAP IT processes, methods, technology, and techniques to conduct requirements validation and PPBE activities. Analyzing, evaluating, coordinating, and integrating DCIO SAP IT's activities and deliverables related to the annual POM review. Leading resource management team and assessing progress of assigned projects or programs and keeping records of schedules, cost estimates and expenditures, monitoring contractor's acquisition development up to production and deployment, planning and coordinating activities of data and resource management and other activities, taking actions to approve contracts, budgets, terms and other conditions related to the contractor, and ensuring maintenance of documentation. Reviewing and providing short notice, quick-reaction analyses of critical programmatic issues and providing data to assist in preparation for legislative hearings, program documentation, briefing packages and read-aheads, Congressional staffer visits, and other events to ensure an integrated and consistent position across DCIO SAP IT and DoD CIO, and the Military Services and DAFAs SAP IT equities, in response to Congressional questions, issues, and requests for information on assigned program/portfolio.

Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level (GG-11) in the federal service. For this position, qualifying experience is defined as: assisting in the development of administrative policies and procedures relating to management systems and responding to administrative inquiries. To qualify at the GG-13 level, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level (GG-12) in the federal service. For this position, qualifying experience is defined as: developing administrative policies and procedures relating to management systems, monitoring action or suspense items for timeliness and completion, and responding to and resolving complex administrative inquiries. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Candidates must describe how they meet the qualifying experience and/or selective placement factor(s) within the body of their resume. All qualifications must be met within 30 days after the closing date of this announcement.

Details.JobSummary: This position is being recruited under 10 USC 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It has been identified as a position necessary to carry out and support the mission of the US Cyber Command. It is in the Professional Work Category at the Full Performance Work Level within the CES Occupational Structure. It is located in the DISA-Joint Service Provider (JPA2).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: If you want to do interesting and challenging work and to make a contribution to national defense, DISA is a great place for you. DISA provides secure and reliable communications and computing support that enable the President and our military forces to communicate globally through voice, video, and data transmission. DISA is a leader within the Federal Government in implementing "people programs" and offers a broad range of quality-of-life and training programs. Go to www.disa.mil for more information. This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. Positions in the Cyber Excepted Service are positions necessary to carry out and support the mission of the United States Cyber Command.
MajorDuties: Develop policies and procedures regarding the administrative work processes and operations. Write, establish, and implement administrative policies and procedures to ensure effective management systems.

Execute the internal management control program for Joint Service Provider (JSP). Function as a communications expert for the organization. Undertake studies and projects that result in significant communication improvements for JSP.

Ensure the coordination, adequacy, and timeliness of all suspense items from the Command Group on staff and Center actions and other various issues. Determine action required for each suspense item and assign to appropriate office.

Keep the Chief and required parties advised of controversial and time-sensitive issues. Maintain a list of current action items and their status. Provide advice and assistance to management concerning office functions and missions.

Serves as the lead project officer for the development and the on-going upgrade of Directorate-wide workflow processes. Analyze the accuracy and validity of the products and provide recommended changes and improvements on an on-going basis

Engage in oversights of a variety of analytical studies and office/administrative services. These services include, travel, training, space management, timekeeping, brief preparation, correspondence preparation and review.

Assign work based on priorities, consideration of the difficultly and requirements of assignments, and the capabilities of employees. Review, accept and reject work products. Give advice to employees on work and administrative matters.
Details.Education: There is no substitution of education for the qualifying experience at the GG-13 grade level

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-14 grade level , if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service: Providing guidance on the development and management of campaign and contingency plans and amplifying instructions for planners. Developing the guidance for, or participating in, the planning and development of theater or functional posture. Creating and implementing doctrine and policies regarding interagency political/military planning. Planning and coordinating large scale meetings with senior level staff where discussion takes place regarding campaign and contingency plans, theater or functional posture, or interagency political/military planning. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent conducts research and analyses, conference management and political­ military planning efforts, database management, plans assessments, and coordination production services in support of J-5/JOWPD. The work includes efforts to develop planning processes, coalitions, and integration concepts.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-5 (Strategic Plans and Policy) proposes strategies, plans, and policy recommendations to the CJCS to support his provision of "best military advice" across the full spectrum of national security concerns to the President and other national leaders and to ensure those recommendations are informed by a larger strategic context coordinated with interagency and alliance partners, account for the view and requirements of the combatant commanders, and assess risk in executing the national Military Strategy.
MajorDuties: As a JOINT PLANNER at the GS-0301-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Represents the Director, Joint Staff J-5 and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs in the development and coordination of campaign and contingency plans with senior staff within and outside the Department of Defense. Serves as an advisor to management on planning and posture effects with DoD and non DoD personnel and provides policy advice and guidance, as needed. Conducts research and analysis, as needed, to support planning and posture efforts and successful project completion. Designs and prepares for planning and posture coordination conferences, working group meetings, and seminars in support of Combatant Commands (CCMD) and DoD planning efforts. Leads or assists with the planning and coordinating of multiple and major interagency working groups, planning cells, military exercise sessions, and war games.
Details.Education: Substitution of education may not be used in lieu of specialized experience for this grade level.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act Chapter 21 of Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C.), Section 2108a, requires Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, at the time they apply for a Federal job, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, assuming the service member is otherwise eligible. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. The service member's military service dates are necessary in order to determine whether he or she meets the definition of "veteran" under 5 U.S.C. 2108(1). The "certification" must reflect the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date of submission. The "certification" must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters and must indicate when your terminal leave will begin (if applicable), your rank, dates of active duty service, the type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable). Further, under paragraph (h) of the rule, agencies are required to verify a qualifying separation from military service prior to appointment, through the DD-214 or other appropriate documentation. Your preference and/or appointment eligibility will be verified prior to appointment. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible." Military members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if member is on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Beginning January 1, 2010, agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level under the provisions of title 5, United States Code. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Submit a copy of your applicable SF-50, along with a statement that provides the following information regarding your most recent political appointment: Position title; Type of appointment (Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES, or Presidential Appointee); Agency; and, Beginning and ending dates of appointment. All qualifications and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.

Details.JobSummary: The incumbent serves as a highly motivated self-starter who works independently and with senior executives at the Office of Secretary of Defense (OSD) or Component levels.as an Executive Assistant for the Executive Director, Force Resiliency (EDFR), Office of Force Resiliency (OFR), OUSD(P&R) supporting OFR and its programs. Duties include managing the correspondence control system; correspondence, records, and administrative management; and implementing programs, policies, and procedures.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (OUSD(P&R))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of Defense, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as the Executive Secretary for the Office of Force Resiliency (OFR) performing a range of direct executive office support for the Executive Director, Force Resilience (EDFR) and OFR's front office staff; serves as the point of contact for coordination, development, and interpretation of policies and coordinates the flow of information among program activities. Provides all executive administrative support functions for the front office; provides direction, advice, and assistance to management and employees on administrative issues and for the automated systems supporting correspondence for the office. Reviews all correspondence/packages for content, accuracy, and completeness; serves as the correspondence control representative and primary point of administrative contact and liaison with external offices and individuals on operational and programmatic matters. Oversees and tracks tasks and requests from the Government Accountability Office (GAO), DoD Inspector General (IG), and Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) for OFR programs and provides guidance for timely and quality submissions. Completes special projects as directed and provides formal and informal, written and oral briefings to senior staff members on various issues and projects, and performs action officer duties in support of OFR functions and requirements.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!

You will oversee coordination and activities for various programs affecting Health Services to include Medical Readiness and Professional Development, Expeditionary Medical Systems, and Medical Logistics.
You will plan and execute technical and administrative functions to include overseeing analysis for new requirements in response to capability gaps and emerging needs.

You will apply mastery level knowledge of the POM process to prepare long-range and short-range planning guidance in accordance with broad agency program policies and objectives.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as the senior Army civilian responsible for coordinating and implementing Army support to Homeland Defense and Civil Support current operations and planning future events, Operational Plans and Contingency Plans.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Plan for and conduct special events (including National Security Special Events, such as the Presidential Inauguration and the State of the Union Address (SOTUA), and Army response to natural and man-made disasters.
Analyze, develop and maintain Homeland Defense/Civil Support Branch Standing Operating Procedures to ensure responsive and appropriate Army support to HD and CS missions.
Ensure close coordination with external organizations (principally the Joint Staff and sister Services) and internal organizations (the Army Staff), Major Command and Army Service Component Commands.
Negotiate with appropriate action offices and various officials to achieve mission objectives.

Oversee Domestic Operations and develop goals and objectives that integrate organization and section objectives in administering Intranet SharePoint, data management, and internet portal systems ensuring functionality and, implementation.
Perform the full range of supervisory duties such as plan the work to be accomplished by subordinates, set and adjust short-term priorities, and prepare schedules for completion of work.
